summary: Give a ceramic vessel readable wall thickness, body/glaze boundaries and decoration depth before adding glossy highlights.
objective: Make a glazed vessel read as a constructed ceramic object with an intentional surface layer.
intent_signals: Make a glazed vessel read as a constructed ceramic object with an intentional surface layer.
example_prompts: Build a painted ceramic teapot with a thick rim, a selected unglazed foot and decoration beneath a satin glaze.

principles: Distinguish body geometry, surface coating and decoration placement. If a design is described as underglaze, place its appearance below the glaze response rather than automatically giving it raised metal-like relief.
Choose the depicted finish: matte, satin, glossy, opaque or translucent treatments are artistic options; no single setting defines all ceramics.
implementation: Model the lip, inner wall, handle attachment and foot in geometry. Mask a glaze boundary only where the selected design has one; do not require every vessel to have an exposed clay band.
Keep glaze roughness independent of the body's broad color variation; test a broad highlight crossing a painted motif so coating response and decoration remain distinct.
Use actual chipped layer geometry only for an intended damaged object. Keep crackle or decoration width in object scale and avoid inflating every painted line through normal detail.
observable_checks: At an oblique rim view, the wall and inner cavity remain understandable even when the glaze catches a large reflection.
A chosen underglaze motif remains beneath a continuous coating highlight rather than behaving like an unrelated glowing sticker.
The exposed foot, if present, contrasts with the coating through finish or boundary structure without requiring a fixed hue.

known_limits: This does not identify firing temperature, historical origin, food safety, glaze chemistry or liquid impermeability of a particular object.
Authored modeling and inspection guidance; no runtime artifact or improvement has been observed for this record.
creative_affordances: Unglazed biscuit, playful opaque glaze and graphic brushwork are valid; glossy realism is optional.

claims.statement: The V&A defines underglaze as ceramic decoration beneath the glaze layer.
claims.scope: Terminology and layer ordering only; no general glaze composition or manufacturing claim.
